text: One lesbian couple’s winding path to marriage leads to a historic first in Bolivia 1 of 6 | Like many newlyweds, Fabiana Justiniano and Scarlett Rocha grow misty-eyed when they reminisce about their wedding day: racing from the civil registry to get their hair and makeup done, dancing in their white dresses late into the night with more than a hundred friends and relatives. Their August 7 wedding was more than a personal milestone. It was a legal one, too: Bolivia’s first same-sex civil marriage - the culmination of a grueling struggle in a religiously and socially conservative nation where the constitution defines marriage as the union of a man and a woman. title: Ukraine war chronicled in 50-metre-long painting
text: Ukraine war chronicled in 50-metre-long painting Image caption, Russell Haines has recalled some of the Ukrainians he has met on his travels to the country through the medium of painting By Maisie Lillywhite Gloucestershire Published 20 August 2026 A 50-metre-long (164ft) painting depicting a city's response to the war in Ukraine is going on display for a month before being taken to the Eastern European country. Gloucester artist Russell Haines has been painting Lines of Resistance, which chronicles the stories of Ukrainian families who found a new home in the city and residents who volunteered to deliver aid. The painting is not finished, as Haines said "the story belongs to more than one artist". During the exhibition, which launches on Thursday, he will invite visitors to add their own words for the people of Ukraine. Ukrainian people will have the opportunity to send messages to Gloucester residents when the painting arrives there. text: Putin Orders Government to Shore Up Russia’s Debt-Laden Regions Aug. 20, 2026 Russia's Finance Ministry. Andrey Nikerichev / Moskva News Agency President Vladimir Putin has ordered the Russian government to stabilize regional finances as local authorities face a combined budget deficit of 1.9 trillion rubles ($22.6 billion) this year. The order comes as the federal government struggles to fill its own budget shortfall, which has reached 6.5 trillion rubles ($77.4 billion). “The stability of regional finances is also the direct responsibility of the federal government and the Finance Ministry,” Putin said at a meeting with senior officials. text: Tula Governor Defends Child After Local Officials Threaten Criminal Charges Over Playground Drawings Aug. 20, 2026 Drawings made by a young girl in the town of Bolokhovo, Tula region. vk.сom The governor of central Russia’s Tula region has come to the defense of a young girl after local officials threatened criminal prosecution over artwork she drew onto a city playground earlier this week. In a post on the VKontakte social media platform, authorities in the town of Bolokhovo said they had filed a police complaint after identifying a child who drew characters from a popular animated series onto the rubber safety surface of a newly renovated playground. title: Putin Visits Newly Unearthed Remains of Dmitry Donskoy
text: Putin Visits Newly Unearthed Remains of Dmitry Donskoy By Reuters Aug. 20, 2026 Vladimir Putin. kremlin.ru President Vladimir Putin on Thursday visited the sarcophagus of medieval warrior prince Dmitry Donskoy, whose remains were recently uncovered during restoration work at Moscow's Cathedral of the Archangel. Lying within the Kremlin fortress, the Orthodox cathedral served as the burial site for more than 40 Russian tsars and princes down the centuries. The body of Grand Prince Donskoy was known to lie there, but its discovery last month in a crypt by the southern wall surprised historians, who had believed it was located elsewhere in the building. Putin lit a candle inside the frescoed cathedral and stood beside the white-stone sarcophagus as experts explained to the president how they had identified the remains as those of the 14th-century prince, the RIA Novosti news agency reported. text: German Spy Agency Opens Hotline for Exiled Russians By Reuters Aug. 20, 2026 REUTERS / Thilo Schmuelgen Germany's domestic intelligence agency has established a dedicated hotline for exile groups and political dissidents facing intimidation, surveillance or physical violence from foreign operatives inside the country, with a key focus on threats emanating from Russia alongside countries like Iran and China. The Federal Office for the Protection of the Constitution (BfV) on Thursday published a brochure advertising the hotline for individuals who have sought refuge in Germany from authoritarian governments. text: Anti-War NGO Reports Rise in Forced Enlistments Across Russia By Mack Tubridy Aug. 20, 2026 A contract service recruitment office in Moscow. Arthur Novosiltsev / Moskva News Agency Idite Lesom (“Get Lost”) , a group that helps Russian men avoid military service, has reported receiving a growing number of complaints from individuals who were forcibly detained and coerced into signing contracts with Russia’s Defense Ministry. Between Aug. 10 and 18, Idite Lesom recorded 14 separate cases from regions across Russia, including Krasnodar, Omsk, Arkhangelsk and the J ewish autonomous district , as well as the republics of Udmurtia and Buryatia. text: Official Who Led Wartime Asset Seizures Quietly Reinstated After Dismissal – Fontanka Aug. 20, 2026 Sergei Bochkarev. ossetia.tv The senior official who spearheaded the Russian government’s wave of private asset seizures since the full-scale invasion of Ukraine has been quietly returned to his job after Prosecutor General Alexander Gutsan reportedly dismissed him last month, the news outlet Fontanka reported Wednesday, citing a source familiar with the matter. The official, Sergei Bochkarev, headed the Civil and Judicial Department of the Prosecutor General’s Office. Under his direction, the government nationalized around 6.5 trillion rubles ($81.45 billion) in private assets since 2022. Bochkarev’s most high-profile targets included Moscow’s Domodedovo Airport , food manufacturer Makfa and gold miner YUGK . In July, sources told the newspaper Kommersant that Gutsan dismissed Bochkarev after the chief prosecutor had publicly criticized him earlier for the mismanagement of confiscated properties, which he warned was undermining efforts to return them to the market. title: Russian Missile and Drone Attack Kills 17 in Kyiv
text: Russian Missile and Drone Attack Kills 17 in Kyiv Aug. 20, 2026 Firefighters in Kyiv battle a blaze that broke out during a Russian attack on Aug. 20, 2026. Ukrainian State Emergency Service Russia n strikes killed 17 people and injured more than 40 in Kyiv and the surrounding region on Thursday as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said a failure by Ukraine's allies to replenish its stock of air defense missiles was costing lives. Ukraine's air force said Russia launched dozens of missiles and 168 drones in the overnight attack. The air force said that nearly 90% of the drones and most of the cruise missiles were downed. It did not specify how many ballistic missiles were launched and whether any were intercepted. The upper floors of a nine-story residential block were destroyed in Kyiv's Solomianskyi district, where the majority of the 15 deaths in the capital occurred, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said. He called for Friday to be observed as a day of mourning. Two other districts suffered damage, Klitschko said, with a school and a children's hospital hit as well as non-residential facilities and warehouses. At least 17 people have been killed as blocks of flats and warehouses were struck across the city overnight, the State Emergency Service of Ukraine said. A children's hospital and school were also damaged, and more than 40 people have been injured, it added. On Thursday, Kyiv's mayor Vitali Klitschko warned residents of Desnyansky and part of the Dnipro districts may experience a disrupted supply of hot water, following the overnight attacks. Gloucester artist Russell Haines has been painting Lines of Resistance, which chronicles the stories of Ukrainian families who found a new home in the city and residents who volunteered to deliver aid. The painting is not finished, as Haines said "the story belongs to more than one artist". During the exhibition, which launches on Thursday, he will invite visitors to add their own words for the people of Ukraine. Ukrainian people will have the opportunity to send messages to Gloucester residents when the painting arrives there. title: Tula Governor Defends Child After Local Officials Threaten Criminal Charges Over Playground Drawings
text: Tula Governor Defends Child After Local Officials Threaten Criminal Charges Over Playground Drawings Aug. 20, 2026 Drawings made by a young girl in the town of Bolokhovo, Tula region. vk.сom The governor of central Russia’s Tula region has come to the defense of a young girl after local officials threatened criminal prosecution over artwork she drew onto a city playground earlier this week. In a post on the VKontakte social media platform, authorities in the town of Bolokhovo said they had filed a police complaint after identifying a child who drew characters from a popular animated series onto the rubber safety surface of a newly renovated playground. Officials threatened to pursue criminal charges against the girl and her parents for vandalism and property destruction unless they voluntarily removed the drawings. “This surface is designed for children’s safety, not artistic expression,” the VKontakte post read. “Damaging public property is an offense for which you will be held legally accountable.” The threat of legal action triggered public backlash online. title: Putin Visits Newly Unearthed Remains of Dmitry Donskoy
text: Putin Visits Newly Unearthed Remains of Dmitry Donskoy By Reuters Aug. 20, 2026 Vladimir Putin. kremlin.ru President Vladimir Putin on Thursday visited the sarcophagus of medieval warrior prince Dmitry Donskoy, whose remains were recently uncovered during restoration work at Moscow's Cathedral of the Archangel. Lying within the Kremlin fortress, the Orthodox cathedral served as the burial site for more than 40 Russian tsars and princes down the centuries. The body of Grand Prince Donskoy was known to lie there, but its discovery last month in a crypt by the southern wall surprised historians, who had believed it was located elsewhere in the building. Putin lit a candle inside the frescoed cathedral and stood beside the white-stone sarcophagus as experts explained to the president how they had identified the remains as those of the 14th-century prince, the RIA Novosti news agency reported. The Russian Orthodox Church announced the discovery on Tuesday, saying the well-preserved remains were nearly complete and belonged to a man of just under 180 cm (5 feet, 11 inches), who had died of natural causes between the ages of 35 and 45. text: Regions Calling: Decoding Putin’s Eastern Odyssey By Leyla Latypova Aug. 20, 2026 Putin boards the missile cruiser Varyag, the flagship of the Pacific Fleet, during a visit to Russia’s Far East. Kremlin.ru Hello and welcome to Regions Calling , your guide to developments from beyond the Russian capital by The Moscow Times. text: German Spy Agency Opens Hotline for Exiled Russians By Reuters Aug. 20, 2026 REUTERS / Thilo Schmuelgen Germany's domestic intelligence agency has established a dedicated hotline for exile groups and political dissidents facing intimidation, surveillance or physical violence from foreign operatives inside the country, with a key focus on threats emanating from Russia alongside countries like Iran and China. The Federal Office for the Protection of the Constitution (BfV) on Thursday published a brochure advertising the hotline for individuals who have sought refuge in Germany from authoritarian governments. Under the initiative, victims of state-sponsored harassment are encouraged to report incidents to help intelligence analysts identify, map and counter foreign operative networks operating in Europe. The BfV indicated in the brochure that information provided by affected individuals could directly assist ongoing investigations and potentially help thwart active threats. Arthur Novosiltsev / Moskva News Agency Idite Lesom (“Get Lost”) , a group that helps Russian men avoid military service, has reported receiving a growing number of complaints from individuals who were forcibly detained and coerced into signing contracts with Russia’s Defense Ministry. Between Aug. 10 and 18, Idite Lesom recorded 14 separate cases from regions across Russia, including Krasnodar, Omsk, Arkhangelsk and the J ewish autonomous district , as well as the republics of Udmurtia and Buryatia. text: Official Who Led Wartime Asset Seizures Quietly Reinstated After Dismissal – Fontanka Aug. 20, 2026 Sergei Bochkarev. ossetia.tv The senior official who spearheaded the Russian government’s wave of private asset seizures since the full-scale invasion of Ukraine has been quietly returned to his job after Prosecutor General Alexander Gutsan reportedly dismissed him last month, the news outlet Fontanka reported Wednesday, citing a source familiar with the matter. The official, Sergei Bochkarev, headed the Civil and Judicial Department of the Prosecutor General’s Office. Under his direction, the government nationalized around 6.5 trillion rubles ($81.45 billion) in private assets since 2022. Bochkarev’s most high-profile targets included Moscow’s Domodedovo Airport , food manufacturer Makfa and gold miner YUGK . In July, sources told the newspaper Kommersant that Gutsan dismissed Bochkarev after the chief prosecutor had publicly criticized him earlier for the mismanagement of confiscated properties, which he warned was undermining efforts to return them to the market. title: Russian Missile and Drone Attack Kills 17 in Kyiv
text: Russian Missile and Drone Attack Kills 17 in Kyiv Aug. 20, 2026 Firefighters in Kyiv battle a blaze that broke out during a Russian attack on Aug. 20, 2026. Ukrainian State Emergency Service Russia n strikes killed 17 people and injured more than 40 in Kyiv and the surrounding region on Thursday as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said a failure by Ukraine's allies to replenish its stock of air defense missiles was costing lives. Ukraine's air force said Russia launched dozens of missiles and 168 drones in the overnight attack. The air force said that nearly 90% of the drones and most of the cruise missiles were downed. It did not specify how many ballistic missiles were launched and whether any were intercepted. The upper floors of a nine-story residential block were destroyed in Kyiv's Solomianskyi district, where the majority of the 15 deaths in the capital occurred, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said. He called for Friday to be observed as a day of mourning. Two other districts suffered damage, Klitschko said, with a school and a children's hospital hit as well as non-residential facilities and warehouses. title: Russia 'purposefully' hit critical infrastructure in latest strikes, Kyiv mayor says
text: Russia 'purposefully' hit critical infrastructure in latest strikes, Kyiv mayor says Figure caption, The Mayor of Kyiv, Vitali Klitschko, tells the BBC Ukraine needs more help from its partners to protect civilians By Imogen James Â and Â Dan Johnson ,Â Ukraine correspondent Published 20 August 2026 Russia's latest attack on Kyiv marks the first time in several months critical infrastructure "was purposefully attacked" in the Ukrainian capital, the city's mayor said. At least 17 people have been killed as blocks of flats and warehouses were struck across the city overnight, the State Emergency Service of Ukraine said. A children's hospital and school were also damaged, and more than 40 people have been injured, it added. On Thursday, Kyiv's mayor Vitali Klitschko warned residents of Desnyansky and part of the Dnipro districts may experience a disrupted supply of hot water, following the overnight attacks. "Specialists are working to restore the damaged infrastructure," he said on Telegram , external . title: United Russia mayor forces Yabloko party candidate to take down banner reading ‘For peace and freedom’
text: Pavel Kharitonenko, a single-mandate candidate from the Yabloko party in the State Duma election, said Vasily Temgenevsky, the mayor of Baikalsk in the Irkutsk region and a member of the United Russia party, has been hindering his campaign. Kharitonenko said his first campaign banner — bearing the slogan “For Peace and Freedom” — was taken down in the city “under pressure” from the mayor. The banner had been hanging at a local market since August 11. “He [Temgenevsky] called business owners and demanded they take down my poster. No argument — that this is official campaign material, that the election commission has been notified of it, and that it was paid for from the candidate’s campaign account, and is therefore legal — could get through to him,” Kharitonenko said. Kharitonenko is one of three candidates registered in the Irkutsk region for single-mandate seats in the State Duma, the lower house of Russia’s parliament, running from Yabloko. Russia’s Supreme Court removed the party’s federal list from the State Duma election. Nationwide, 126 Yabloko candidates are running for single-mandate seats. title: Russian Missile and Drone Attack Kills 17 in Kyiv
text: Russian Missile and Drone Attack Kills 17 in Kyiv Aug. 20, 2026 Firefighters in Kyiv battle a blaze that broke out during a Russian attack on Aug. 20, 2026. Ukrainian State Emergency Service Russia n strikes killed 17 people and injured more than 40 in Kyiv and the surrounding region on Thursday as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said a failure by Ukraine's allies to replenish its stock of air defense missiles was costing lives. Ukraine's air force said Russia launched dozens of missiles and 168 drones in the overnight attack. The air force said that nearly 90% of the drones and most of the cruise missiles were downed. It did not specify how many ballistic missiles were launched and whether any were intercepted. The upper floors of a nine-story residential block were destroyed in Kyiv's Solomianskyi district, where the majority of the 15 deaths in the capital occurred, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said. He called for Friday to be observed as a day of mourning. Two other districts suffered damage, Klitschko said, with a school and a children's hospital hit as well as non-residential facilities and warehouses. title: Ukraine war chronicled in 50-metre-long painting
text: Ukraine war chronicled in 50-metre-long painting Image caption, Russell Haines has recalled some of the Ukrainians he has met on his travels to the country through the medium of painting By Maisie Lillywhite Gloucestershire Published 20 August 2026 A 50-metre-long (164ft) painting depicting a city's response to the war in Ukraine is going on display for a month before being taken to the Eastern European country. Gloucester artist Russell Haines has been painting Lines of Resistance, which chronicles the stories of Ukrainian families who found a new home in the city and residents who volunteered to deliver aid. The painting is not finished, as Haines said "the story belongs to more than one artist". During the exhibition, which launches on Thursday, he will invite visitors to add their own words for the people of Ukraine. Ukrainian people will have the opportunity to send messages to Gloucester residents when the painting arrives there. text: Tula Governor Defends Child After Local Officials Threaten Criminal Charges Over Playground Drawings Aug. 20, 2026 Drawings made by a young girl in the town of Bolokhovo, Tula region. vk.сom The governor of central Russia’s Tula region has come to the defense of a young girl after local officials threatened criminal prosecution over artwork she drew onto a city playground earlier this week. In a post on the VKontakte social media platform, authorities in the town of Bolokhovo said they had filed a police complaint after identifying a child who drew characters from a popular animated series onto the rubber safety surface of a newly renovated playground. Officials threatened to pursue criminal charges against the girl and her parents for vandalism and property destruction unless they voluntarily removed the drawings. “This surface is designed for children’s safety, not artistic expression,” the VKontakte post read. “Damaging public property is an offense for which you will be held legally accountable.” The threat of legal action triggered public backlash online. text: Putin Visits Newly Unearthed Remains of Dmitry Donskoy By Reuters Aug. 20, 2026 Vladimir Putin. kremlin.ru President Vladimir Putin on Thursday visited the sarcophagus of medieval warrior prince Dmitry Donskoy, whose remains were recently uncovered during restoration work at Moscow's Cathedral of the Archangel. Lying within the Kremlin fortress, the Orthodox cathedral served as the burial site for more than 40 Russian tsars and princes down the centuries. The body of Grand Prince Donskoy was known to lie there, but its discovery last month in a crypt by the southern wall surprised historians, who had believed it was located elsewhere in the building. Putin lit a candle inside the frescoed cathedral and stood beside the white-stone sarcophagus as experts explained to the president how they had identified the remains as those of the 14th-century prince, the RIA Novosti news agency reported. The Russian Orthodox Church announced the discovery on Tuesday, saying the well-preserved remains were nearly complete and belonged to a man of just under 180 cm (5 feet, 11 inches), who had died of natural causes between the ages of 35 and 45. text: Ukraine war chronicled in 50-metre-long painting Image caption, Russell Haines has recalled some of the Ukrainians he has met on his travels to the country through the medium of painting By Maisie Lillywhite Gloucestershire Published 20 August 2026 A 50-metre-long (164ft) painting depicting a city's response to the war in Ukraine is going on display for a month before being taken to the Eastern European country. Gloucester artist Russell Haines has been painting Lines of Resistance, which chronicles the stories of Ukrainian families who found a new home in the city and residents who volunteered to deliver aid. The painting is not finished, as Haines said "the story belongs to more than one artist". During the exhibition, which launches on Thursday, he will invite visitors to add their own words for the people of Ukraine. Ukrainian people will have the opportunity to send messages to Gloucester residents when the painting arrives there. title: Putin Orders Government to Shore Up Russia’s Debt-Laden Regions
text: Putin Orders Government to Shore Up Russia’s Debt-Laden Regions Aug. 20, 2026 Russia's Finance Ministry. Andrey Nikerichev / Moskva News Agency President Vladimir Putin has ordered the Russian government to stabilize regional finances as local authorities face a combined budget deficit of 1.9 trillion rubles ($22.6 billion) this year. The order comes as the federal government struggles to fill its own budget shortfall, which has reached 6.5 trillion rubles ($77.4 billion). “The stability of regional finances is also the direct responsibility of the federal government and the Finance Ministry,” Putin said at a meeting with senior officials. Finance Minister Anton Siluanov said Russia’s regions currently owe a combined 3.3 trillion rubles ($39.3 billion), equal to about 17% of their own revenue. Around two-thirds of that debt consists of low-interest loans from the federal government. The rest is borrowed on the market and carries much higher interest rates. Putin ordered the government to provide 100 billion rubles ($1.2 billion) to the regions facing the most serious financial problems. title: Ukraine war chronicled in 50-metre-long painting
text: Ukraine war chronicled in 50-metre-long painting Image caption, Russell Haines has recalled some of the Ukrainians he has met on his travels to the country through the medium of painting By Maisie Lillywhite Gloucestershire Published 20 August 2026 A 50-metre-long (164ft) painting depicting a city's response to the war in Ukraine is going on display for a month before being taken to the Eastern European country. Gloucester artist Russell Haines has been painting Lines of Resistance, which chronicles the stories of Ukrainian families who found a new home in the city and residents who volunteered to deliver aid. The painting is not finished, as Haines said "the story belongs to more than one artist". During the exhibition, which launches on Thursday, he will invite visitors to add their own words for the people of Ukraine. Ukrainian people will have the opportunity to send messages to Gloucester residents when the painting arrives there. text: Advertising Germany records 14,000 heat-related deaths this summer as heatwaves scorch Europe Europe Berlin has recorded roughly 14,000 heat-related deaths this summer, official data showed Thursday. Europe has experienced a spike in heat-related mortality as the worst-hit countries grapple with historically high temperatures exacerbated by human-driven climate change. Around 9,600 of those deaths were recorded in one week in late June when Germany baked in temperatures of over 40°C, according to the Robert Koch Institute. In a post on the VKontakte social media platform, authorities in the town of Bolokhovo said they had filed a police complaint after identifying a child who drew characters from a popular animated series onto the rubber safety surface of a newly renovated playground. text: Russian Missile and Drone Attack Kills 17 in Kyiv Aug. 20, 2026 Firefighters in Kyiv battle a blaze that broke out during a Russian attack on Aug. 20, 2026. Ukrainian State Emergency Service Russia n strikes killed 17 people and injured more than 40 in Kyiv and the surrounding region on Thursday as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said a failure by Ukraine's allies to replenish its stock of air defense missiles was costing lives. Ukraine's air force said Russia launched dozens of missiles and 168 drones in the overnight attack. The air force said that nearly 90% of the drones and most of the cruise missiles were downed. It did not specify how many ballistic missiles were launched and whether any were intercepted. The upper floors of a nine-story residential block were destroyed in Kyiv's Solomianskyi district, where the majority of the 15 deaths in the capital occurred, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said. He called for Friday to be observed as a day of mourning. title: Ukraine war chronicled in 50-metre-long painting
text: Ukraine war chronicled in 50-metre-long painting Figure caption, Ukraine war captured in 50-metre-long painting By Maisie Lillywhite Gloucestershire Published 20 August 2026 A 50-metre-long (164ft) painting depicting a city's response to the war in Ukraine is going on display for a month before being taken to the Eastern European country. Gloucester artist Russell Haines has been painting Lines of Resistance, which chronicles the stories of Ukrainian families who found a new home in the city and residents who volunteered to deliver aid. The painting is not finished, as Haines said "the story belongs to more than one artist". During the exhibition, which launches on Thursday, he will invite visitors to add their own words for the people of Ukraine. Ukrainian people will have the opportunity to send messages to Gloucester residents when the painting arrives there.
